• Keep UI (view + controller) separate from model/service so the logic can be unit-tested without starting JavaFX (MVC/MVVM). Load resources with getClass().getResource("/com/.../view/main.fxml") (never relative file paths).

interviewQA: Why does "JavaFX runtime components are missing" appear?
The JavaFX modules are not on the module path or not added with --add-modules, or the main class extends Application in a classpath launch; add the modules or use a separate launcher class.
How do you add JavaFX to a Maven project?
Add org.openjfx javafx-controls/javafx-fxml dependencies and the javafx-maven-plugin, then run mvn javafx:run.
Why separate model/service from controllers?
So business logic can be tested without the JavaFX toolkit and the UI can change independently (MVC/MVVM).

topics.name: Application Lifecycle, Application Class, Stage and Scene Graph

beginner.content:
The Application lifecycle

• Application.launch(args) starts the toolkit and calls, in order: init() (on the launcher thread, no UI creation, a good place for loading configuration), start(Stage primaryStage) (on the JavaFX Application Thread: build and show the UI) and, after the last window closes (when Platform.isImplicitExit()) or Platform.exit(), stop() (release resources, close pools and DB connections). launch blocks until the application exits and can be called only once per JVM. getParameters() gives command-line arguments.

intermediate.content:
Stage, Scene and the scene graph

• Stage = a window (the primary stage is given to start; create more for dialogs). Scene = the content of a stage: holds one root node and optional width/height, fill, stylesheets. Scene graph = a tree of Nodes: Parent nodes (Group, Region → panes, controls) have children; Shape, ImageView, Canvas are leaves. A node can have only one parent and can be in only one scene. Stage styles: DECORATED, UNDECORATED, TRANSPARENT, UTILITY; modality NONE, WINDOW_MODAL, APPLICATION_MODAL.

expert.content:
Application thread, parameters and quitting

• Platform.runLater schedules code on the JavaFX Application Thread; Platform.exit() ends the app (calls stop); Platform.setImplicitExit(false) keeps the app alive with no windows (system tray apps). Command line: getParameters().getNamed()/getRaw(). Host services: getHostServices().showDocument(url) opens the browser. Splash screens: Preloader (or an early undecorated stage). Scene graph changes of a live scene must happen on the Application Thread.

interviewQA: What is the JavaFX application lifecycle?
launch() starts the toolkit; init() runs on the launcher thread, start(Stage) on the JavaFX Application Thread to build the UI, and stop() runs when the application exits to release resources.
Stage vs Scene?
A Stage is a window; a Scene is the content of a stage and holds the root node of the scene graph.
Why create UI in start() rather than init()?
init() runs on the launcher thread, not the JavaFX Application Thread; UI objects such as Stage must be created on the Application Thread.

topics.name: Label, Button, TextField, PasswordField, TextArea, CheckBox, RadioButton and ToggleGroup

beginner.content:
Text and button controls

• Label (non-editable text, optional graphic, wrapText, labelFor mnemonic), Button (setOnAction, setDefaultButton(true) reacts to Enter, setCancelButton(true) to Esc, setGraphic), TextField (single line: getText, setPromptText, textProperty()), PasswordField (masked; do not keep the password string longer than needed), TextArea (multi-line, setWrapText, setPrefRowCount).

intermediate.content:
CheckBox, RadioButton and ToggleGroup

• CheckBox (selected/unselected, optional indeterminate with setAllowIndeterminate(true)); RadioButton belongs to a ToggleGroup so only one is selected: use setUserData to attach a value, and listen to selectedToggleProperty(). ToggleButton is the push-style equivalent.

expert.content:
Form validation pattern

• Build forms with binding rather than manual enable/disable code: Bindings.createBooleanBinding over several inputs gives one "valid" property; show inline error labels via visibleProperty().bind(...); validate on focus loss and on submit. For serious forms use a validation library (ControlsFX, Validatorfx) or your own small validator.

interviewQA: How do RadioButtons work together?
They share a ToggleGroup so only one can be selected; read selectedToggleProperty() or getSelectedToggle().getUserData().
How do you disable a Save button until the form is valid?
Bind its disableProperty to the negation of a boolean binding created from the input properties.
Why use PasswordField instead of TextField?
It masks the characters and prevents cut/copy of the text; still avoid keeping the password in memory or logs longer than needed.

topics.name: ComboBox, ChoiceBox, ListView, TreeView, DatePicker, ProgressBar and Slider

beginner.content:
Selection controls

• ComboBox<T> (drop-down; optionally editable; setItems(ObservableList), valueProperty(), setCellFactory and setConverter(StringConverter) to show objects nicely), ChoiceBox<T> (simpler, short lists), ListView<T> (scrollable list; SelectionMode.MULTIPLE, setCellFactory for custom rows), TreeView<T> (hierarchical: TreeItem with children, setShowRoot(false)), DatePicker (LocalDate), ProgressBar/ProgressIndicator (0..1 or indeterminate -1), Slider (min, max, value, ticks, valueChanging).

intermediate.content:
TreeView

• A TreeView shows TreeItem<T>s with expanded state; build lazily by overriding isLeaf()/getChildren() in a custom TreeItem for big trees (file systems). Use setCellFactory for icons, and getSelectionModel().selectedItemProperty() for navigation menus or module outlines.

expert.content:
Custom cells with cell factories

• Lists, combo boxes, tables and trees render items through cells, reused as you scroll (virtualised). A cellFactory returns a ListCell whose updateItem(item, empty) must always set or clear text and graphic (cells are recycled: forgetting the empty branch shows stale content).

interviewQA: ComboBox vs ChoiceBox?
ComboBox is richer (editable, custom cells, converters, more items); ChoiceBox is a simple selection of a few items.
Why must updateItem handle the empty case?
Cells are reused while scrolling, so you must clear text and graphic when the cell is empty, otherwise stale content from another item appears.
How do you display objects in a ComboBox?
Provide a StringConverter (and/or a cellFactory/buttonCell) that maps the object to the text shown.

topics.name: MenuBar, ToolBar, TabPane, TableView Introduction, Dialog and Alert

beginner.content:
MenuBar, ToolBar and TabPane

• MenuBar contains Menus of MenuItem/CheckMenuItem/RadioMenuItem/SeparatorMenuItem with accelerator (KeyCombination.keyCombination("Shortcut+S"); on macOS setUseSystemMenuBar(true)). ToolBar holds buttons/separators and overflows into a chevron. TabPane hosts Tabs (setClosable, TabClosingPolicy, selectionModelProperty(), lazy content).

intermediate.content:
Dialog and Alert

• Alert (AlertType.INFORMATION/WARNING/ERROR/CONFIRMATION) and the generic Dialog<R> are modal windows: showAndWait() returns an Optional of the pressed ButtonType (or custom result). TextInputDialog and ChoiceDialog collect a value. Set the owner (initOwner(stage)) so the dialog centres on the window. Do not block long operations inside the handler.

expert.content:
TableView at a glance and picking controls

• TableView<S> shows tabular data with TableColumn<S,T>s fed by an ObservableList<S> (covered in depth in section 8). Choosing controls: few fixed options → radio buttons/choice box; many options → combo box; large collections → list/table (virtualised); hierarchy → tree; dates → DatePicker; numbers in a range → Slider/Spinner; long operations → ProgressBar bound to a Task. Remember accessibility: labels, mnemonics, tab order (focusTraversable), tooltips (Tooltip.install).

interviewQA: What does Alert.showAndWait() return?
An Optional<ButtonType> holding the button the user pressed (empty if closed without choosing); it blocks while keeping the event loop running.
How do you add a keyboard shortcut to a menu item?
Set its accelerator, e.g. KeyCombination.keyCombination("Shortcut+S"), where Shortcut maps to Ctrl or Cmd per platform.
TabPane closing policies?
UNAVAILABLE (no close buttons), SELECTED_TAB (only the selected tab can be closed) and ALL_TABS.

topics.name: HBox, VBox, BorderPane, FlowPane, TilePane and StackPane

beginner.content:
How layout works

• A layout pane (a Region subclass) positions and sizes its children using each child's min / pref / max sizes and the pane's rules; resizable nodes can grow (Priority.ALWAYS/SOMETIMES). Layout is recomputed whenever sizes or children change (a layout pass per pulse). Never set absolute positions unless you use Pane/Group deliberately: let panes do the work so the UI adapts to window size, fonts and DPI.

intermediate.content:
BorderPane, FlowPane, TilePane and StackPane

PaneBehaviourUse for
BorderPaneTop, bottom, left, right, centre (centre takes the rest)Application shell: menu top, navigation left, content centre, status bottom
FlowPaneWraps children like text when width runs outTag lists, button groups, thumbnails
TilePaneEqual-sized cells wrapping in rows/columnsImage galleries, dashboards of cards
StackPaneChildren layered on top of each other (z-order = child order), centred by defaultOverlays, badges, loading spinner over content, custom controls

expert.content:
Spacing, margin, padding and alignment

• Padding = space inside a pane around its children; margin = space around a child set via the pane's static method (VBox.setMargin(node, insets)); spacing/hgap/vgap = gaps between children; alignment = where children sit inside the pane (Pos). Use CSS (-fx-padding, -fx-spacing) to keep spacing in the stylesheet.

interviewQA: HBox vs VBox vs StackPane?
HBox lays out children in a row, VBox in a column, StackPane layers children on top of each other.
What is BorderPane good for?
The classic application shell with top, left, right, bottom and a centre region that takes the remaining space.
Padding vs margin?
Padding is space inside a container around all its children; margin is space around a single child, set through the parent pane.

topics.name: GridPane, AnchorPane, Layout Constraints and Responsive Layouts

beginner.content:
GridPane

• GridPane arranges children in rows and columns: add(node, col, row, colSpan, rowSpan), hgap/vgap, and per-column/row constraints: ColumnConstraints (percentWidth, hgrow, minWidth/prefWidth/maxWidth) and RowConstraints. Ideal for forms (labels left, fields right).

intermediate.content:
AnchorPane and constraints

• AnchorPane anchors children to edges with distances (setTopAnchor, setLeftAnchor ...); anchoring two opposite edges stretches the child: good for FXML designs from Scene Builder and for pinning toolbars/status bars. Prefer container panes for new layouts; use AnchorPane for an overlay or when drawing precisely. Layout constraints (static setters: GridPane.setConstraints, HBox.setHgrow, BorderPane.setAlignment, VBox.setMargin) are stored in the child's properties and read by the parent.

expert.content:
Responsive layouts

• Make the UI adapt to window size: use grow priorities instead of fixed sizes; wrap content with FlowPane/TilePane; bind sizes to the scene (pane.prefWidthProperty().bind(scene.widthProperty().multiply(0.3))); switch layouts by width with a listener (scene.widthProperty() → show/hide the sidebar, change a GridPane column count, toggle a style class like compact); use SplitPane for user-resizable areas and ScrollPane (fitToWidth) for overflow; set minimum stage size. Test with different DPI scaling and fonts.

interviewQA: Why use GridPane for forms?
Rows and columns keep labels and fields aligned, and column constraints let the field column grow while the label column stays compact.
What does setManaged(false) do?
The node is ignored by its parent's layout (takes no space), usually combined with setVisible(false) to hide it completely.
How do you make a layout responsive?
Use grow priorities and wrapping panes, bind sizes to the scene, switch layouts or style classes from width listeners and set sensible minimum sizes.

topics.name: Event Handling Fundamentals: Handlers, Lambdas, Action, Mouse and Keyboard Events

beginner.content:
The event model

• An Event has a source, a target (the node it happened to), a type (MouseEvent.MOUSE_CLICKED, KeyEvent.KEY_PRESSED, ActionEvent.ACTION ...) and can be consumed. Register EventHandler<T> with setOnXxx(...) (one handler per property: setOnAction, setOnMouseClicked) or addEventHandler(type, handler) (several). Handlers are functional interfaces, so use lambdas or method references.

intermediate.content:
Mouse and keyboard events

• Mouse: MOUSE_PRESSED/RELEASED/CLICKED (getClickCount(), getButton()), MOUSE_MOVED/DRAGGED, MOUSE_ENTERED/EXITED (hover), getX()/getSceneX()/getScreenX() coordinates, ScrollEvent, ContextMenuEvent. Keyboard: KEY_PRESSED/RELEASED (getCode() → KeyCode, modifiers isControlDown(), isShortcutDown()) and KEY_TYPED (getCharacter()). The node must be focused to receive key events: install shortcuts on the Scene or with scene.getAccelerators().

expert.content:
Handling best practices

• Keep handlers short: delegate to controller/service methods; never block the Application Thread inside a handler (network, database, sleep) - start a Task instead; remove listeners/handlers from long-lived sources to avoid leaks; use weak listeners (WeakEventHandler, WeakChangeListener) when needed; prefer binding to wiring events that copy values; centralise shortcuts.

interviewQA: setOnAction vs addEventHandler?
setOnXxx holds a single convenience handler per event property; addEventHandler registers any number of handlers for an event type.
Why do key events sometimes not arrive?
Key events go to the focused node; if nothing relevant is focused register the handler on the Scene (or use accelerators).
Why shouldn't a handler perform a long operation?
Handlers run on the JavaFX Application Thread; blocking it freezes the whole UI, so use a background Task.

topics.name: Event Filters, Bubbling, Capturing and Custom Events

beginner.content:
Event delivery: capturing then bubbling

• When an event occurs, JavaFX builds the event dispatch chain from the Stage down to the target node (root → ... → target). Delivery has two phases: capturing (event travels from the root down to the target; event filters run) then bubbling (back up from the target to the root; event handlers run). Calling event.consume() stops further propagation. This lets a parent intercept (filter) or react to (handler) events of its children.

intermediate.content:
Filters vs handlers, consuming events

Event filterEvent handler
PhaseCapturing (parent before child)Bubbling (child before parent)
RegisteraddEventFilter(type, h)addEventHandler(type, h) / setOnXxx
Typical useIntercept/block events before the target sees them (disable input while loading, restrict characters)React to events, optionally centralising child events at a parent
ConsumeChild never receives the eventParents above do not receive it

expert.content:
Custom events

• Subclass Event, define an EventType (child of Event.ANY), then node.fireEvent(new CourseSelectedEvent(course)) and listen with addEventHandler. Good for custom controls that expose their own events and for decoupling controllers; for application-wide messaging prefer an event bus or shared model/properties. Cast carefully: handlers receive the specific event type.

interviewQA: Explain event capturing and bubbling in JavaFX.
Events travel down the dispatch chain from the stage to the target during capturing (filters run) and back up during bubbling (handlers run); consume() stops propagation.
Event filter vs event handler?
Filters run during capturing and can intercept events before the target sees them; handlers run during bubbling for reacting to events.
How do you define a custom event?
Extend Event with a static EventType, fire it with node.fireEvent and register handlers with addEventHandler for that type.

topics.name: JavaFX Properties, Observable Values and Property Types

beginner.content:
Why properties?

• A JavaFX property is an observable wrapper of a value: it notifies listeners when the value changes and can be bound to other properties. Almost every UI attribute is a property (textProperty, selectedProperty, widthProperty, disableProperty). Domain models can expose properties so tables and forms update automatically. Naming convention: getX()/setX() + xProperty().
• Hierarchy: Observable (invalidation) → ObservableValue<T> (getValue, change listeners) → ReadOnlyProperty → Property<T> (bind, setValue, bindBidirectional) → implementations SimpleStringProperty, SimpleIntegerProperty, SimpleDoubleProperty, SimpleBooleanProperty, SimpleObjectProperty<T>, SimpleListProperty, SimpleMapProperty, plus ReadOnlyXxxWrapper for read-only exposure.

intermediate.content:
A property-based model class

• Expose the property accessor, and also plain getter/setter for convenience and for frameworks. Keep the model free of UI types. For tables you need xProperty() methods (or PropertyValueFactory reflection via getters).

expert.content:
ObservableList, ObservableMap and extractors

• FXCollections.observableArrayList() returns an ObservableList that notifies ListChangeListeners about additions, removals, replacements, permutations and updates (change.next() loop). ObservableMap/ObservableSet exist too. Extractors make the list fire update events when a property of an element changes (needed for filtered/sorted lists reacting to property changes). FilteredList and SortedList are views over a source list.

interviewQA: What is a JavaFX property?
An observable wrapper around a value that notifies listeners on change and supports binding; UI attributes and model fields are exposed as properties.
What is an extractor in an ObservableList?
A function returning the Observables of an element whose changes should trigger update events of the list, so FilteredList/SortedList and cells react to property changes.
Why use ReadOnlyBooleanWrapper?
It lets the class modify the value internally while exposing only a read-only property to clients.

topics.name: Property Binding: Unidirectional, Bidirectional, Bindings API, Change and Invalidation Listeners

beginner.content:
Unidirectional and bidirectional binding

• Unidirectional target.bind(source): the target always follows the source and cannot be set manually while bound (RuntimeException); unbind() releases it. Bidirectional a.bindBidirectional(b): both stay in sync (form fields ↔ model). Types must match, or convert with bindBidirectional(stringProp, numberProp, new NumberStringConverter()).

intermediate.content:
High-level and low-level Bindings API

• Fluent API on properties: text.length().greaterThan(3), a.add(b), price.multiply(quantity), name.isEmpty(), flag.and(other).not(), when(cond).then(x).otherwise(y). Bindings utility: Bindings.format("%.2f", total), Bindings.concat, Bindings.when, Bindings.createStringBinding(Callable, dependencies...) for custom computed values, Bindings.size(list), Bindings.isEmpty(list), Bindings.selectString for nested paths. Bindings are lazy: recomputed when read after being invalidated.

expert.content:
Change listeners vs invalidation listeners

ChangeListenerInvalidationListener
Signaturechanged(observable, oldValue, newValue)invalidated(observable)
FiresWhen the value actually changesWhen the value becomes invalid (may not have changed; lazy, only once until re-read)
EvaluationForces the new value to be computed (eager)Does not compute (lazy)
UseReact with old/new valuesCheap "something changed" signal (redraw)
• Memory leaks: a listener on a long-lived property (a model, a service) keeps the listener's owner (a controller, a node) reachable. Remove listeners when the view closes, or use WeakChangeListener/WeakInvalidationListener (keep a strong reference to the real listener yourself). Bindings hold only weak references from the source side, so bind is leak-safe but addListener is not.

interviewQA: Unidirectional vs bidirectional binding?
Unidirectional makes the target follow the source and prevents manual setting; bidirectional keeps two properties synchronised in both directions, ideal for form fields and model properties.
ChangeListener vs InvalidationListener?
A ChangeListener receives old and new values when the value changes and forces evaluation; an InvalidationListener only signals invalidation and is lazy and cheaper.
How can property listeners cause memory leaks?
A listener registered on a long-lived property keeps its owner reachable; remove listeners when the view is disposed or use weak listeners.

topics.name: Introduction to FXML, Syntax, FXMLLoader and Controllers

beginner.content:
What is FXML?

• FXML is an XML-based markup language for describing the JavaFX scene graph declaratively. It separates view (layout and controls: .fxml) from logic (controller class). Benefits: readable structure, designer tooling (Scene Builder), easier collaboration, less boilerplate. Elements are JavaFX classes (imported with <?import ...?>), attributes are properties, nested elements are children or property values.
codeExamples:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<?import javafx.geometry.Insets?>
<?import javafx.scene.control.*?>
<?import javafx.scene.layout.*?>

<VBox xmlns="http://javafx.com/javafx" xmlns:fx="http://javafx.com/fxml"
      fx:controller="com.javaschoollab.tracker.ui.CourseFormController" spacing="12" prefWidth="420">
    <padding><Insets top="16" right="16" bottom="16" left="16"/></padding>
    <Label text="New course" styleClass="title"/>
    <TextField fx:id="titleField" promptText="Course title"/>
    <ComboBox fx:id="levelCombo" promptText="Level" maxWidth="Infinity"/>
    <HBox spacing="8" alignment="CENTER_RIGHT">
        <Button text="Cancel" onAction="#onCancel" cancelButton="true"/>
        <Button fx:id="saveButton" text="Save" onAction="#onSave" defaultButton="true"/>
    </HBox>
</VBox>

intermediate.content:
Controllers, fx:id, @FXML and onAction

• fx:controller names the controller class; the loader instantiates it (public no-arg constructor) and injects nodes whose fx:id matches a field annotated @FXML (private is fine with @FXML; needs opens ... to javafx.fxml in a module). Event attributes onAction="#handler" call a method (annotated @FXML if non-public) taking the event or nothing. initialize() (no-arg, @FXML) is called after injection: wire bindings, items and listeners there; the constructor runs before injection (fields are still null). The Initializable interface (initialize(URL, ResourceBundle)) is the older alternative.

expert.content:
FXMLLoader

• new FXMLLoader(url) then load() returns the root node and creates the controller (getController() afterwards). A loader instance loads once: create a new loader per load. Options: setController(obj) (when the FXML has no fx:controller), setControllerFactory(cls -> ...) (create controllers with dependencies: constructor injection, Spring), setResources(ResourceBundle) for i18n (%key in FXML), setRoot + setController(this) for custom components (fx:root). Always use getResource paths; a null URL gives LoadException: Location is not set.

interviewQA: When is initialize() called?
After the FXML has been loaded and @FXML fields injected, so UI setup that needs the nodes belongs there rather than in the constructor.
Why is my @FXML field null?
The fx:id does not match the field name, the field lacks @FXML, the controller was not created by FXMLLoader (created with new), or you access it in the constructor before injection.
How can FXML controllers receive dependencies?
Use a controller factory on the FXMLLoader (constructor injection or Spring), or pass data through setters after load.

topics.name: Scene Builder, Controller Communication and Reusable FXML Components

beginner.content:
Scene Builder

• Scene Builder (Gluon) is a visual drag-and-drop editor for FXML: palette of controls, hierarchy panel, inspector for properties/layout/code (fx:id, event handlers, controller class), CSS preview. Typical workflow: design the layout in Scene Builder, set the controller class and fx:ids, then use View → Show Sample Controller Skeleton to generate the @FXML fields and handlers. Integrate with IntelliJ/Eclipse ("Open in Scene Builder"). Keep FXML files small (one screen or component per file) and avoid logic in FXML (expression bindings only for simple things).
codeExamples:
<!-- FXML expression binding and references -->
<Label text="${titleField.text}"/>                                  <!-- one-way binding to another node's property -->
<fx:define><Insets fx:id="pad" top="8" right="8" bottom="8" left="8"/></fx:define>
<VBox padding="${pad}"/>
<fx:include source="toolbar.fxml" fx:id="toolbar"/>                    <!-- include another FXML; controller injected as toolbarController -->

intermediate.content:
Controller communication

• Options: (1) Parent holds child controller: with <fx:include fx:id="toolbar"> a field @FXML private ToolbarController toolbarController; is injected (name = fx:id + Controller). (2) Pass data via setters/methods after load() using getController(). (3) Shared model/services (observable properties in a model both controllers bind to): best for decoupling. (4) Callbacks (Consumer<Course> passed to the child). (5) Event bus (custom events, a simple pub/sub, or an app-level event bus). Avoid static references between controllers.

expert.content:
Reusable FXML components (fx:root)

• A custom component that is both a control and its own controller: FXML root <fx:root type="VBox">; the Java class extends VBox and in its constructor loads the FXML with setRoot(this) and setController(this). The component can then be used in other FXML files as <CourseCard course="..."/> and by code. Add public properties (courseProperty()) and custom events for a clean API.
codeExamples:
<!-- course-card.fxml -->
<?import javafx.scene.control.*?><?import javafx.scene.layout.*?>
<fx:root type="VBox" xmlns="http://javafx.com/javafx" xmlns:fx="http://javafx.com/fxml" spacing="4" styleClass="card">
    <Label fx:id="title" styleClass="card-title"/>
    <Label fx:id="meta" styleClass="muted"/>
    <Button text="Open" onAction="#open"/>
</fx:root>

public class CourseCard extends VBox {
    @FXML private Label title; @FXML private Label meta;
    private final ObjectProperty<Course> course = new SimpleObjectProperty<>();

    public CourseCard() {
        FXMLLoader loader = new FXMLLoader(getClass().getResource("course-card.fxml"));
        loader.setRoot(this); loader.setController(this);
        try { loader.load(); } catch (IOException e) { throw new UncheckedIOException(e); }
        course.addListener((o, a, c) -> { title.setText(c.title()); meta.setText(c.lessons() + " lessons"); });
    }
    public ObjectProperty<Course> courseProperty() { return course; }
    @FXML private void open() { fireEvent(new CourseSelectedEvent(course.get())); }
}
// usage in code: new CourseCard() ; in FXML: <CourseCard fx:id="card"/>

interviewQA: How do two FXML controllers communicate?
Through shared model objects with observable properties, parent-child controller references from fx:include, callbacks or an event bus; avoid static references.
What is fx:root used for?
Building reusable custom components where the Java class is both the root node and the controller of its FXML.
What does Scene Builder generate for you?
A visual editor produces the FXML and a sample controller skeleton with @FXML fields and handler stubs matching the fx:id values and onAction attributes.

topics.name: JavaFX CSS: Inline vs External, Selectors, Style Classes, IDs and Pseudo-Classes

beginner.content:
JavaFX CSS

• JavaFX has its own CSS dialect: properties are prefixed -fx- (-fx-background-color, -fx-text-fill, -fx-font-size, -fx-padding, -fx-border-radius, -fx-effect: dropshadow(...)). The default type selector is the node's style class (.button, .label, .text-field), not its Java class name. Inline style: node.setStyle("-fx-text-fill: red;") (highest priority; hard to maintain). External stylesheet: scene.getStylesheets().add(url) or FXML stylesheets="@app.css".

intermediate.content:
Selectors, style classes, IDs and pseudo-classes

SelectorExampleMeaning
Style class.cardNodes with getStyleClass().add("card")
ID#saveButtonNode with setId("saveButton") or FXML id
Descendant.card .labelLabels inside a card
Child.toolbar > .buttonDirect children only
Pseudo-class:hover, :focused, :selected, :disabled, :pressed, :armed, :empty, :odd/:even (cells)State-based styling
Substructure.combo-box .arrow-button, .table-view .column-headerInternal parts of a control (see the Modena CSS reference)
Multiple.button.primaryBoth classes
• Custom pseudo-classes: node.pseudoClassStateChanged(PseudoClass.getPseudoClass("error"), true) then .text-field:error { ... }: model UI state in code, style in CSS.

expert.content:
Precedence, looked-up colours and debugging

• Order of precedence (low → high): the JavaFX default (user agent) stylesheet (Modena) < Application.setUserAgentStylesheet < stylesheets of the Scene < stylesheets of parents (Parent.getStylesheets()) < inline styles. Within a stylesheet: specificity (ID > class > type), then later rules win. Looked-up colours: define -fx-base/-fx-accent/custom variables on .root and derive others with derive(color, -20%), ladder(); change the whole theme by editing the root variables. Debug with ScenicView (inspect the scene graph, style classes, CSS) and -Djavafx.pseudoClassOverrideEnabled; check the log for "CSS Error parsing" warnings.

interviewQA: Inline vs external CSS?
Inline styles (setStyle) have the highest precedence and are for dynamic one-offs; external stylesheets keep styling reusable and maintainable and should be the default.
How do you target a specific state, e.g. an invalid text field?
Define a custom pseudo-class, toggle it with pseudoClassStateChanged and style it with a :error selector in CSS.
Which tool inspects JavaFX CSS at runtime?
ScenicView shows the scene graph, style classes, IDs and applied CSS of a running application.

topics.name: Themes, Custom Fonts, Backgrounds and Borders, Responsive Styling and Dark Mode

beginner.content:
Themes, backgrounds and borders

• Built-in themes: Application.setUserAgentStylesheet(Application.STYLESHEET_MODENA) (default) or STYLESHEET_CASPIAN; JavaFX 22+ adds Platform.Preferences colour scheme detection. Third-party themes: AtlantaFX, JMetro, BootstrapFX, MaterialFX. Backgrounds: -fx-background-color (multiple colours, linear-gradient(...), radial-gradient), -fx-background-image, -fx-background-radius, -fx-background-insets. Borders: -fx-border-color, -fx-border-width, -fx-border-radius, -fx-border-style; effects: -fx-effect: dropshadow(...). In Java: Background/Border objects.

intermediate.content:
Custom fonts

• Load a bundled font with Font.loadFont(getClass().getResourceAsStream("/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf"), 14) before the scene is shown (the family name is then available in CSS), or declare it in CSS with @font-face { src: url("fonts/Inter.ttf"); }. Provide fallbacks (-fx-font-family: "Inter", "Segoe UI", sans-serif). Use icon fonts (Ikonli: FontAwesome, Material) for icons: new FontIcon("fas-save"). Mind font licences.

expert.content:
Responsive styling and dark mode

• Dark mode: keep colours as variables on .root and switch by toggling a style class on the root or swapping the theme stylesheet at runtime. Responsive styling: toggle classes (compact, wide) from scene width listeners and write CSS per class; use relative units (em) and the root font size to scale text; honour HiDPI (JavaFX scales automatically; supply 2x images). Persist the user's theme choice in Preferences.

interviewQA: How do you implement dark mode in JavaFX?
Define colours as variables on .root, provide light and dark stylesheets (or classes) and switch the scene stylesheet at runtime, remembering the choice in Preferences.
How do you use a custom font?
Load it with Font.loadFont before showing the scene (or @font-face) and reference its family name in -fx-font-family with fallbacks.
What is the default JavaFX theme?
Modena, applied as the user agent stylesheet; Caspian is the legacy theme.

topics.name: TableView, TableColumn, PropertyValueFactory and Observable Data

beginner.content:
TableView basics

• TableView<S> shows rows of type S from an ObservableList<S> (setItems); each TableColumn<S,T> has a cell value factory that extracts a value (as an ObservableValue<T>) from a row. Table cells are virtualised, so millions of rows are fine. Set setColumnResizePolicy(TableView.CONSTRAINED_RESIZE_POLICY_FLEX_LAST_COLUMN) (or CONSTRAINED_RESIZE_POLICY_ALL_COLUMNS), setPlaceholder(...) for empty tables.

intermediate.content:
PropertyValueFactory vs lambdas

• new PropertyValueFactory<>("title") uses reflection: it looks for titleProperty(), else getTitle() (read-only wrapper, no automatic updates). Disadvantages: strings are not checked by the compiler, break on refactoring, and in modular apps the model package must be opens ... to javafx.base. Prefer lambda factories returning the property (type safe, live updates). For plain records/immutable models: cell -> new ReadOnlyStringWrapper(cell.getValue().title()) or new SimpleStringProperty(...).

expert.content:
Observable data collections and updating the table

• Modify the ObservableList (add/remove/set) and the table updates automatically; updating an element's property updates its cells if the cell value factory returns the property; for plain getters changes are not seen: call table.refresh() or replace the item. Modify the list on the Application Thread (or build a new list in the background and setAll on the UI thread). For bulk updates use setAll/addAll (one change event) instead of many add calls.

interviewQA: PropertyValueFactory vs lambda cell value factory?
PropertyValueFactory finds a property/getter by name using reflection and is fragile; a lambda returning the property is type safe, refactor friendly and live-updating.
Why doesn't my table update when I change an object?
The cell value factory must return an observable property; with getters or plain values call refresh() or replace the item in the list.
Why is TableView fast with many rows?
It virtualises rows, creating cells only for visible rows and reusing them while scrolling.

topics.name: Sorting, Filtering, Searching, Pagination, Selection and Editable Tables

beginner.content:
Sorting, filtering and searching

• Click a column header to sort; the table sorts the list through table.getSortOrder()/comparator. For filtering wrap the source list: FilteredList<S> filtered = new FilteredList<>(items, p -> true), update filtered.setPredicate(...) when the search text changes; for sorting a filtered list wrap in SortedList and bind its comparator to the table's comparator: sorted.comparatorProperty().bind(table.comparatorProperty()), then table.setItems(sorted).

intermediate.content:
Pagination and row selection

• Pagination control with a page factory returning a node for each page index: show a table of a slice (items.subList(from, to)) or query the database page-by-page (LIMIT/OFFSET, keyset). Selection: table.getSelectionModel() (setSelectionMode(MULTIPLE), getSelectedItem(), getSelectedItems(), selectedItemProperty(), setCellSelectionEnabled(true) for cell selection); bind buttons to selection (deleteButton.disableProperty().bind(table.getSelectionModel().selectedItemProperty().isNull())); double-click rows with a row factory.

expert.content:
Editable tables and custom cell factories

• Editing: table.setEditable(true), then a column's cell factory from TextFieldTableCell.forTableColumn(), ComboBoxTableCell, CheckBoxTableCell, ChoiceBoxTableCell; commit with column.setOnEditCommit(e -> e.getRowValue().setTitle(e.getNewValue())) (validate here; for property-backed models the default commit writes to the property). Custom cell factories render anything in a cell: badges, progress bars, buttons, icons. Always handle empty in updateItem; do not create heavy objects per update; reuse nodes held by the cell.

interviewQA: How do you filter and sort a TableView?
Wrap the source ObservableList in a FilteredList (set a predicate), wrap that in a SortedList whose comparator is bound to the table comparator and set the SortedList as table items.
How do you make cells editable?
Set the table and column editable with a cell factory such as TextFieldTableCell and commit changes in setOnEditCommit or by property binding.
What is a row factory used for?
Customising TableRow behaviour and style, e.g. double-click to open, context menus or row styling by state.

topics.name: Opening New Windows, Switching Scenes, Modal Windows and Window Events

beginner.content:
Opening new windows

• Create another Stage with its own Scene and call show(); set owner (initOwner(parent)) and modality (initModality(Modality.APPLICATION_MODAL | WINDOW_MODAL | NONE)) before showing; showAndWait() blocks the caller until the window closes (nested event loop) and is perfect for modal forms that return a result. Position relative to the owner, set a title and icon.

intermediate.content:
Switching scenes and content

• Two approaches: (1) replace the Scene of the stage: stage.setScene(next) (loses window state such as maximised/size unless handled); (2) swap the content of a fixed shell: keep a BorderPane/StackPane root and call shell.setCenter(loadView("courses")): preferred (single scene, shared menu/toolbar/CSS, easy transitions and back-stack). Build a small router/navigator class: it loads FXML views by name, caches or recreates them, and keeps a history stack.

expert.content:
Menu and tab navigation, passing data, window events

• Menu navigation: MenuItem actions call the navigator; tab-based: a TabPane with a tab per module (open on demand, select existing tab if already open). Passing data between controllers: via the controller (loader.getController().setX()), a shared model/service, a navigation parameter map in the navigator, or a dependency-injected context object. Window events: setOnCloseRequest (confirm unsaved changes; consume() to veto), setOnShowing/OnShown/OnHiding/OnHidden, focusedProperty, iconifiedProperty, maximizedProperty; persist window size/position in Preferences.

interviewQA: Modal window vs non-modal?

A modal stage blocks input to its owner (WINDOW_MODAL) or all application windows (APPLICATION_MODAL) until closed; non-modal windows can be used independently. showAndWait pauses the caller until it closes.
Why swap content instead of scenes?
A single scene with a shell layout keeps window state, menus and CSS and enables transitions; replacing the scene resets more state.
How do you stop a window from closing with unsaved data?
Handle setOnCloseRequest, ask the user and call event.consume() to cancel closing.

topics.name: The JavaFX Application Thread, UI Thread Restrictions and Platform.runLater

beginner.content:
The JavaFX Application Thread

• All live scene graph changes and event handlers run on one thread, the JavaFX Application Thread (FX thread). Blocking it (sleep, JDBC, HTTP, big loops) freezes the entire UI. Touching a live node from another thread throws IllegalStateException: Not on FX application thread. Rule: do long work on background threads, then hand results back to the FX thread. Platform.isFxApplicationThread() checks the current thread.

intermediate.content:
Platform.runLater and its pitfalls

• Platform.runLater(Runnable) queues the runnable on the FX thread. Pitfalls: flooding the queue (calling it thousands of times a second for progress updates makes the UI lag: coalesce updates, use an AtomicReference + one pending runnable, or Task.updateProgress which coalesces for you); it is asynchronous (code after it runs first); exceptions inside are not propagated to the caller; use PlatformImpl.runAndWait-style helpers (a FutureTask + runLater) if you must wait for a result; in tests, the toolkit must be started.

expert.content:
Common symptoms

SymptomCauseFix
Window "Not Responding", no repaintLong work in a handler or start()Move to Task
Not on FX application threadUI change from a worker threadPlatform.runLater or Task callbacks
UI lags while a task reports progressToo many runLater callsThrottle / use updateProgress
Deadlock when waiting for runLater result on the FX threadget() on the FX threadNever block the FX thread
App does not exitNon-daemon worker threadsDaemon threads or shut pools in stop()
codeExamples: Thread t = new Thread(task, "import"); t.setDaemon(true); t.start();          // daemon: does not keep the JVM alive

interviewQA: Why can't you update the UI from a background thread?
The scene graph is not thread-safe and is accessed only by the JavaFX Application Thread; changes elsewhere throw IllegalStateException or corrupt state, so use Platform.runLater or Task callbacks.
What is Platform.runLater?
It schedules a Runnable to execute later on the JavaFX Application Thread, used to hand results from worker threads to the UI.
Why does the UI freeze during a long handler?
Handlers run on the single FX thread; while it is busy no events are processed and nothing repaints.

topics.name: Task<V>, Service<V>, Progress, Cancellation and Exception Handling

beginner.content:
Task<V>

• Task<V> (javafx.concurrent) is a one-shot background job that implements Runnable, Future and Worker: you implement call() (runs on the worker thread), and observe properties updated safely on the FX thread: stateProperty (READY, SCHEDULED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, CANCELLED, FAILED), valueProperty, progressProperty, messageProperty, titleProperty, exceptionProperty, runningProperty. Callbacks setOnSucceeded/Failed/Cancelled/Running run on the FX thread. Inside call() use updateProgress(done, total), updateMessage, updateValue (these are throttled and marshalled for you) and check isCancelled().

intermediate.content:
Service<V> and executors

• A Service<V> is a reusable task factory: override createTask(); start() runs it, restart() cancels and runs again, cancel(), reset(); it exposes the same properties of the current task and uses a shared daemon thread pool (or your own setExecutor). ScheduledService repeats on a schedule (polling) with setPeriod, setRestartOnFailure, setBackoffStrategy.
TaskService
RunsOnce (cannot be restarted)Many times (restart/reset)
ThreadYou start it (Thread/executor)Managed (executor)
Typical useOne-off operation (import file)Reusable operation tied to the UI (refresh, search, poll)
Creationnew Task<>() { call() }Subclass with createTask()

expert.content:
Exception handling, cancellation and CompletableFuture integration

• Exceptions thrown in call() move the task to FAILED; read getException() in setOnFailed (not thrown to the FX thread, so an unhandled failure is silent if you don't observe it). Set a default handler: Thread.setDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler. Cancellation is cooperative: cancel() interrupts the thread, so check isCancelled() in loops and handle InterruptedException by restoring the interrupt and returning. CompletableFuture: run work with supplyAsync(..., executor) and move to the FX thread with .thenAcceptAsync(r -> ..., Platform::runLater) (use a custom executor with runLater); handle errors with exceptionally/handle. Virtual threads (Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) are fine for blocking I/O tasks.

interviewQA: Task vs Service?

A Task is a one-shot background job; a Service creates a new Task each time it is started or restarted, so it is reusable and manages threading, ideal for repeatable UI operations like search or refresh.
How do you report progress from a background task?
Call updateProgress and updateMessage inside call(); bind progress bars and labels to the Task properties, which update safely on the FX thread.
How do you handle exceptions and cancellation in a Task?
Observe the FAILED state or exceptionProperty/setOnFailed, and for cancellation check isCancelled() and handle InterruptedException cooperatively.
How do you combine CompletableFuture with JavaFX?
Run the work asynchronously and continue with an executor that delegates to Platform.runLater so UI updates occur on the FX thread.

topics.name: JDBC Integration, MySQL/PostgreSQL, CRUD, Prepared Statements and Connection Pooling

beginner.content:
JDBC in a JavaFX application

• Desktop apps talk to databases with JDBC (MySQL mysql-connector-j, PostgreSQL org.postgresql:postgresql, or embedded SQLite/H2). Connection URL examples: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/tracker, jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/tracker?useSSL=true. Rules: never run JDBC on the FX thread (use Task/Service), always use PreparedStatement with parameters (prevents SQL injection), close resources with try-with-resources, do not hard-code credentials (environment variables/config file; a desktop app cannot keep a database password secret: prefer an API in front of the database for distributed clients).

intermediate.content: CRUD operations and prepared statements

expert.content:
Connection pooling with HikariCP

• Opening a connection is expensive; use a pool (HikariCP) created once at startup and closed in Application.stop(). Desktop apps need small pools (2-5). Handle offline/connection errors gracefully (retry, message, read-only mode).

interviewQA: Why use PreparedStatement?
It sends parameters separately from the SQL text, preventing SQL injection and allowing statement reuse and caching.
Why use a connection pool in a desktop app?
It avoids the cost of opening a connection per operation and bounds concurrent connections; create it once and close it in stop().
Why must JDBC calls run off the FX thread?
They block; running them on the FX thread freezes the UI, so use Task/Service and update the UI on completion.

topics.name: DAO and Repository Patterns, Transactions and Database Error Handling

beginner.content:
DAO and Repository patterns

• DAO: an interface per entity hiding SQL (CourseDao with findAll/findById/save/delete); Repository: a domain-oriented collection abstraction (CourseRepository.findPublished()) possibly composing several DAOs. Controllers depend on the interface, not JDBC: you can swap implementations (JDBC, JPA, REST client, in-memory fake for tests). Add a service layer for business rules and transactions; map rows to immutable records, and convert to observable view models in the UI layer.

intermediate.content:
Transaction management

• Group several statements into one atomic unit: con.setAutoCommit(false), run statements on the same connection, commit(), rollback() in the catch, restore auto-commit, close. Wrap in a small helper so services do not repeat the boilerplate. Use batching (addBatch/executeBatch) for imports. Choose isolation if needed (setTransactionIsolation). With JPA/Hibernate or Spring use @Transactional.

expert.content:
Database error handling in the UI

• Catch SQLException at the service/task boundary and translate it into domain exceptions (DuplicateCourseException for SQLState 23505 (PostgreSQL) / error 1062 (MySQL), DatabaseUnavailableException for connection failures 08xxx). Show friendly messages (not stack traces) via an Alert, log details, offer retry; keep the UI responsive with a progress indicator; never swallow exceptions silently; mind that a Task failure is silent unless observed.

interviewQA: DAO vs Repository?
A DAO wraps access to a table/data source; a Repository models a domain collection of aggregates with domain-oriented queries; both hide persistence behind an interface.
How do you perform several statements atomically in JDBC?
Turn off auto-commit, execute on one connection, commit on success and rollback on failure, then restore auto-commit.
How should database errors be shown to users?
Translate SQLExceptions to domain exceptions and show friendly messages with retry options while logging technical details.

topics.name: JavaFX with Spring Context: Dependency Injection, FXML Controller Factory and Bean Integration

beginner.content:
Why combine JavaFX and Spring Boot?

• JavaFX creates Application and FXML controllers itself, so Spring does not manage them by default. Integrating Spring gives dependency injection, Spring Data JPA, transactions, configuration properties, RestClient/WebClient and Spring Security for a desktop client. The recipe: start the Spring ApplicationContext in init() (off the UI thread), register the FXML controller factory so controllers are Spring beans, and close the context in stop(). Two classes: a Spring Boot application class (@SpringBootApplication) and a JavaFX Application subclass; start JavaFX from main.

intermediate.content:
FXML controller factory and Spring beans

• Make controllers Spring-managed prototypes (@Component @Scope("prototype"), a fresh instance per FXML load) and tell the loader to ask Spring: loader.setControllerFactory(context::getBean). Controllers then use constructor injection of services. A StageInitializer listens for StageReadyEvent and loads the main FXML. A reusable FxmlLoader/ViewLoader bean (ApplicationContext + factory) keeps loading code in one place.

Service layer, Spring Data JPA and Hibernate

• Put business logic in @Service classes with @Transactional (called from Tasks, never on the FX thread). Spring Data JPA repositories (interface CourseRepository extends JpaRepository<CourseEntity, Long>) and Hibernate need no extra JavaFX code: set spring.datasource.*, spring.jpa.open-in-view is irrelevant (no web). Map entities to view models/DTOs before the UI: lazy associations accessed after the transaction cause LazyInitializationException, and JPA entities are not JavaFX properties. Use Flyway for schema versions and H2/SQLite for offline desktop use.

expert.content:
REST API integration and Spring Security

• A desktop client often calls a backend: use RestClient (Spring 6.1) or WebClient/HttpClient inside Tasks with timeouts and error mapping. Authenticate with OAuth2/JWT: obtain a token (login screen or device flow), keep it in memory, attach it with an interceptor, refresh on 401, and store refresh tokens in the OS keychain (not plain files). Spring Security (method security, SecurityContext) can protect services; store the current Authentication in a session object and remember the security context is thread-bound: propagate it to background threads (DelegatingSecurityContextExecutor).

Application configuration

• Use @ConfigurationProperties for settings (API URL, theme, window defaults), profiles for dev/prod (application-dev.yml), and a per-user settings file/Preferences for UI state. Fail fast on invalid configuration, log startup details, and keep secrets out of the jar. Startup time matters for desktop apps: avoid web auto-configuration, lazy-init heavy beans and show a splash/preloader while Spring starts in init(). Test controllers with Spring by using @SpringBootTest and TestFX or by unit-testing services only.

interviewQA: How do you integrate JavaFX with Spring Boot?

Start the Spring context in Application.init(), publish a stage-ready event from start() and use an FXMLLoader controller factory (context::getBean) so controllers are Spring beans; close the context in stop().
Why make FXML controllers prototype-scoped?
FXMLLoader needs a new controller instance per loaded view; a singleton would share UI state across views.
What problem occurs when passing JPA entities to the UI?
Lazy associations accessed after the transaction end throw LazyInitializationException and entities are not observable; map to view models inside the transaction.

topics.name: Custom Controls and Components, Canvas API and GraphicsContext

beginner.content:
Custom controls and components

• Levels of customisation: (1) compose existing nodes into a reusable Region/VBox subclass or an FXML fx:root component (most common); (2) style a control with CSS and cell factories; (3) a full custom control = Control subclass + Skin (SkinBase) + CSS (behaviour/skin separation; for libraries); (4) draw yourself on a Canvas or Region with shapes. Expose properties (StyleableProperty for CSS), events and a sensible default size (computePrefWidth).

intermediate.content:
Canvas API and GraphicsContext

• Canvas is an immediate-mode drawing surface (a single node, fast for many shapes: games, charts, signal plots, whiteboards). Get GraphicsContext gc = canvas.getGraphicsContext2D(): setFill/setStroke, fillRect, strokeLine, fillOval, fillText, paths (beginPath/moveTo/lineTo/stroke), drawImage, transforms (save/translate/rotate/scale/restore), clipping, blend modes. The canvas does not retain shapes: redraw everything when needed; resize by listening to the parent size. For animation use AnimationTimer.

expert.content:
When to choose which

NeedUse
Reusable form/card widgetComposite node or fx:root FXML component
Library-quality control with theming and behaviour separationControl + Skin
Thousands of animated primitivesCanvas (immediate mode)
A few interactive shapes (hit-testing, events, CSS)Scene graph shapes (Rectangle, Circle, Path)

interviewQA: Canvas vs scene graph shapes?

Canvas is immediate-mode drawing on one node, fast for many primitives but with no retained objects or hit-testing; scene graph shapes are retained nodes with events and CSS but heavier in large numbers.
How do you create a reusable component?
Compose existing nodes in a Region/VBox subclass (or fx:root FXML) exposing properties and events; use Control+Skin for library-grade controls.

topics.name: Charts, Animations, Transitions, Timeline and Media Playback

beginner.content:
Charts

• javafx.scene.chart: LineChart, BarChart, PieChart, AreaChart, ScatterChart, BubbleChart, StackedBarChart. Axes: CategoryAxis, NumberAxis. Data: XYChart.Series<X,Y> with XYChart.Data (observable: updates animate). Style via CSS (.chart-series-line, .default-color0.chart-bar); add tooltips to data nodes; for dense data downsample or use a Canvas chart library (ChartFX, FXGraphs).

intermediate.content:
Animations, transitions and Timeline

• Transitions animate one aspect with a duration: FadeTransition, TranslateTransition, ScaleTransition, RotateTransition, FillTransition, PathTransition, combined with SequentialTransition/ParallelTransition, PauseTransition (delay). Timeline animates any property with KeyFrames and KeyValues (and Interpolator.EASE_BOTH), supports setCycleCount(INDEFINITE), setAutoReverse, or runs code at intervals (a clock). AnimationTimer is a per-frame callback for games. Animations run on the FX thread; stop them when the view closes.

expert.content:
Media playback

• javafx-media: Media (URL: file/http; supported formats: MP3, AAC, WAV, MP4/H.264 with AAC, HLS), MediaPlayer (play/pause/stop/seek, volumeProperty, currentTimeProperty, setOnReady/OnEndOfMedia/OnError), MediaView (video surface). AudioClip is for short sound effects (low latency). Keep a strong reference to the player (it can be garbage-collected and stop playing). Codec support is limited: check errors.

interviewQA: Transition vs Timeline?
Transitions animate a specific node aspect with a fixed duration and compose well; a Timeline animates arbitrary properties or runs code at keyframes and supports cycles and easing.
Why might a MediaPlayer stop unexpectedly?
It was garbage-collected because no strong reference was kept; store it in a field.
How do you add tooltips to chart data?
After adding data, install a Tooltip on each XYChart.Data node (d.getNode()).

topics.name: Drag and Drop, Clipboard, File and Directory Choosers, Printing and WebView

beginner.content:
Drag and drop

• Source: setOnDragDetected → startDragAndDrop(TransferMode.COPY/MOVE/LINK), put data in a ClipboardContent. Target: setOnDragOver (call acceptTransferModes if the dragboard has the expected content), setOnDragDropped (read the dragboard, setDropCompleted(true)), setOnDragDone on the source. Works for text, files, images and custom DataFormats; the classic use is dropping files onto the window and reordering list cells.

intermediate.content:
Clipboard, FileChooser and DirectoryChooser

• Clipboard.getSystemClipboard(): setContent(ClipboardContent), getString(), hasImage(), getFiles(). FileChooser (setTitle, setInitialDirectory, getExtensionFilters().add(new ExtensionFilter("CSV", "*.csv")), showOpenDialog / showOpenMultipleDialog / showSaveDialog(window) returns null if cancelled) and DirectoryChooser (showDialog). Do file I/O off the FX thread; remember the last directory in Preferences.

expert.content:
Printing and WebView

• Printing: PrinterJob job = PrinterJob.createPrinterJob(), job.showPrintDialog(window), job.printPage(node), job.endJob(); scale to the page via Printer.getDefaultPrinter().getDefaultPageLayout(); for reports, generate a PDF (Apache PDFBox, OpenPDF, JasperReports) rather than printing nodes. WebView (javafx-web) embeds a WebKit browser: getEngine().load(url) / loadContent(html), executeScript("..."), Java ↔ JavaScript bridge (JSObject.setMember("app", javaObject) with a public class), getLoadWorker().stateProperty(). Treat loaded content as untrusted (do not expose powerful Java objects to remote pages), keep it up to date, and mind the extra memory/size.

interviewQA: How do you accept files dropped on a window?
Handle setOnDragOver to accept TransferMode.COPY when the dragboard has files and setOnDragDropped to read db.getFiles() and call setDropCompleted(true).
What does FileChooser.showOpenDialog return when cancelled?
null, so always null-check the result.
What are the risks of exposing Java objects to WebView pages?
Remote or injected scripts could call them; only expose minimal bridges to trusted local content.

topics.name: JUnit 5, Mockito, Controller Testing, TestFX UI and Event Testing

beginner.content:
Test strategy for JavaFX

• Keep logic out of controllers (MVVM/MVP: a view model with properties and commands) so most tests are plain JUnit 5 + Mockito without the toolkit. Test properties and bindings directly (they are plain Java objects). Test controllers by injecting mocked services and calling handlers; test UI behaviour end-to-end with TestFX. UI tests are slower and flakier: keep them few and stable.

intermediate.content:
Controller testing and TestFX

• TestFX (org.testfx:testfx-junit5) starts the toolkit, shows your stage and lets a FxRobot click, type, drag and query nodes by CSS selector or text: clickOn("#saveButton"), write("JavaFX"), lookup(".table-row-cell").queryAll(), verifyThat("#status", hasText("Saved")) (TestFX matchers via Hamcrest or FxAssert). Use @Start to build the UI, give nodes stable IDs, and wait for async work with WaitForAsyncUtils.waitForFxEvents() or Awaitility. For CI run headless with Monocle (-Dtestfx.headless=true -Dglass.platform=Monocle -Dmonocle.platform=Headless -Dprism.order=sw) or xvfb on Linux.

expert.content:
Event, threading and background-task tests

• Fire events programmatically (button.fire(), node.fireEvent(new MouseEvent(...))) in a test running on the FX thread (Platform.runLater + CountDownLatch or TestFX helpers). Test Task/Service logic by extracting the work into a plain method and testing it; if you must test the Task, start the toolkit once (Platform.startup) and wait for completion. Make time injectable (Clock) and avoid Thread.sleep in tests.

interviewQA: How do you make JavaFX code testable?
Move logic into view models/services (plain objects with properties), inject dependencies, keep controllers thin and use TestFX only for a few end-to-end UI tests.
How do you run TestFX tests in CI?
Headless with Monocle (or xvfb on Linux) and software rendering flags.
How do you wait for async UI work in tests?
WaitForAsyncUtils.waitForFxEvents, Awaitility or latches instead of Thread.sleep.

topics.name: Debugging FXML, Threading Issues, Memory Leaks and Performance Profiling

beginner.content:
Debugging FXML and the scene graph

• Common FXML errors: LoadException: Location is not set (wrong resource path), ... is not a valid type (missing <?import?>), fx:controller not found/Can not set ... field to null (id mismatch, missing @FXML, package not opensed to javafx.fxml), Controller value already specified, handler method not found (name or signature). Read the root cause at the bottom of the stack trace and the line number inside the FXML. Inspect a running UI with ScenicView (node tree, bounds, CSS, properties) and -Djavafx.verbose/-Dprism.verbose=true.

intermediate.content:
Threading issues

• Frozen UI → long work on the FX thread (take a thread dump: jstack/jcmd Thread.print, look at "JavaFX Application Thread"). Not on FX application thread → UI updated from a worker. Deadlock → waiting on the FX thread for a result that needs the FX thread (runLater().get()). Lost exceptions → Tasks/futures failing silently: observe failures and set a default uncaught-exception handler. Race conditions → mutating the same ObservableList from several threads (mutate only on the FX thread).

expert.content:
Memory leaks and performance profiling

• Leak sources: listeners/bindings on long-lived properties (model.xProperty().addListener(...) from a closed view), static references to controllers/stages, unstopped Timeline/AnimationTimer/executors, event handlers on the scene, cached images, un-disposed WebView/MediaPlayer, growing lists. Detect: heap histogram (jcmd GC.class_histogram), heap dump + Eclipse MAT/VisualVM (find who retains a closed Controller), watch memory after opening/closing a view repeatedly. Fix: remove listeners, use weak listeners, bind instead of copying, null references, stop animations in dispose().
• Performance: keep the scene graph small (avoid thousands of nodes: use virtualised ListView/TableView or Canvas), avoid heavy effects (DropShadow on many nodes, large blurs), cache static nodes (setCache(true), CacheHint.SPEED), batch list updates (setAll), debounce listeners, avoid expensive work in updateItem, run work off the FX thread, load big images in the background (new Image(url, w, h, true, true, true)), use -Dprism.verbose, pulse logger -Djavafx.pulseLogger=true, VisualVM/JFR for CPU and allocation profiling.

interviewQA: How do you find a memory leak in a JavaFX app?
Open and close a view repeatedly, take a heap dump and inspect who retains old controllers/nodes, typically listeners, static references, timelines or executors, then remove or weakly reference them.
What causes "Unable to make field private ... accessible" with FXML?
In a modular app the controller package is not opened to javafx.fxml; add opens ... to javafx.fxml in module-info.java.
How do you diagnose a frozen JavaFX UI?
Take a thread dump and look at what the JavaFX Application Thread is executing; move that work to a background task.

topics.name: Maven and Gradle Packaging, Java Modules, module-info.java and JavaFX Module Configuration

beginner.content:
Packaging options

• Classpath fat jar (maven-shade/Gradle shadow): simple but JavaFX needs a non-Application launcher class as Main-Class and platform-specific JavaFX jars. Modular app (module-info.java): run with the module path; enables jlink custom runtimes and jpackage installers. Native installers: jpackage. The JavaFX jars are platform-classified (win/linux/mac): the Maven plugin picks the right one for the build machine; for cross-platform fat jars include all classifiers or build on each OS (CI matrix).
codeExamples:
<!-- Maven: build a runnable fat jar (classpath mode) -->
<plugin>
  <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId><artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId><version>3.5.1</version>
  <executions><execution><phase>package</phase><goals><goal>shade</goal></goals>
    <configuration><transformers><transformer implementation="org.apache.maven.plugins.shade.resource.ManifestResourceTransformer">
      <mainClass>com.javaschoollab.tracker.Launcher</mainClass></transformer></transformers></configuration>
  </execution></executions>
</plugin>

intermediate.content:
Java modules and module-info.java

• A module declares what it requires and what it exports/opens. For JavaFX: requires javafx.controls; requires javafx.fxml;, exports the package containing the Application class (the launcher accesses it), and opens packages to javafx.fxml (controllers) and javafx.base (PropertyValueFactory/reflection). Other typical requires: java.sql, java.prefs, java.logging, javafx.web, javafx.media, javafx.swing. Non-modular libraries become automatic modules (name from the jar/Automatic-Module-Name); some libraries (Spring, Hibernate) do not play well with strict modules: many JavaFX+Spring apps run on the classpath instead.

expert.content:
JavaFX module configuration and common pitfalls

ErrorCause and fix
Error: JavaFX runtime components are missingLaunching a classpath app whose main class extends Application: add a separate Launcher class or use the module path/--add-modules
Module javafx.controls not foundDependency missing or module path wrong
InaccessibleObjectException for FXML fieldsopens ... to javafx.fxml
Location is not set in a jarResource path/package wrong; resources must be on the module's package path and opensed if loaded reflectively from another module
Works on Windows, fails on Linux/Mac in a fat jarPlatform-specific JavaFX native libraries missing from the jar

interviewQA: What should module-info.java contain for a JavaFX FXML app?
requires javafx.controls and javafx.fxml, exports the package with the Application class and opens controller (and model) packages to javafx.fxml/javafx.base.
Why do fat jars need a separate Launcher class?
If the main class extends Application the JVM checks for JavaFX modules before the classpath is set up and reports "runtime components are missing"; a plain launcher class avoids that.

topics.name: jlink, jpackage, Native Installers, Application Signing and Cross-Platform Deployment

beginner.content:
jlink: a custom runtime

• jlink builds a minimal JRE containing only the modules your app needs (plus the JavaFX modules): a 40-80 MB runtime instead of a full JDK, no separate Java installation for users. Requires a modular app (or jdeps --ignore-missing-deps to find modules and a plugin like badass-jlink for non-modular). Options: --add-modules, --compress=zip-6, --strip-debug, --no-header-files, --no-man-pages, --launcher tracker=com.javaschoollab.tracker/com.javaschoollab.tracker.App.
codeExamples:
jdeps --module-path libs --print-module-deps --ignore-missing-deps target/app.jar
jlink --module-path "$JAVA_HOME/jmods:libs" --add-modules com.javaschoollab.tracker --output build/runtime \
      --strip-debug --compress=zip-6 --no-header-files --no-man-pages \
      --launcher tracker=com.javaschoollab.tracker/com.javaschoollab.tracker.App
build/runtime/bin/tracker

intermediate.content:
jpackage and native installers

• jpackage (JDK 14+, stable in 16) creates a native installer or app image bundling your jar and a runtime: Windows exe/msi (needs WiX Toolset), macOS dmg/pkg/app-image, Linux deb/rpm. Common options: --name, --app-version, --vendor, --icon (.ico/.icns/.png), --input, --main-jar/--module, --main-class, --runtime-image (from jlink), --java-options "-Xmx512m", --win-menu, --win-shortcut, --win-dir-chooser, --win-upgrade-uuid (stable across versions so upgrades replace old installs), --file-associations, --resource-dir (custom installer resources). jpackage builds for the OS it runs on: use CI runners per platform.
codeExamples:
jpackage --type msi --name "Course Tracker" --app-version 1.2.0 --vendor "JavaSchoolLab" --icon src/main/resources/icons/app.ico \
         --module-path "libs;mods" --module com.javaschoollab.tracker/com.javaschoollab.tracker.App \
         --runtime-image build/runtime --dest dist --win-menu --win-shortcut --win-dir-chooser \
         --win-upgrade-uuid 6f9a2a3c-1d55-4a3e-9a6b-3c1f1a2b3c4d --java-options "-Xmx512m"

# macOS
jpackage --type dmg --name "Course Tracker" --input target/libs --main-jar tracker.jar --main-class com.javaschoollab.tracker.Launcher --icon app.icns --mac-package-identifier com.javaschoollab.tracker
# Linux
jpackage --type deb --name course-tracker --input target/libs --main-jar tracker.jar --main-class com.javaschoollab.tracker.Launcher --linux-shortcut

expert.content:
Application signing and cross-platform deployment

• Signing proves who built the installer and avoids "unknown publisher" warnings: Windows code-signing certificate with signtool (EV certificates remove SmartScreen warnings faster), macOS Developer ID certificate + --mac-sign + notarisation (notarytool) required to open on current macOS, Linux package signing (GPG for repos). Keep certificates in CI secrets, never in the repo. Cross-platform: build per OS in a CI matrix (GitHub Actions: windows-latest, macos-latest, ubuntu-latest), choose the right JavaFX classifier, test installers on clean VMs, provide auto-update (e.g. a version check + download, or tools such as Conveyor, install4j, update4j), handle per-user data directories (%APPDATA%, ~/Library/Application Support, ~/.config), log to a user-writable location, and test HiDPI and different fonts. Versioning: semantic versions, a changelog and stable upgrade IDs.

interviewQA: What are jlink and jpackage?
jlink creates a minimal custom Java runtime with only the required modules; jpackage bundles the app and a runtime into a native installer (exe/msi, dmg/pkg, deb/rpm).
Can you build a Windows installer on Linux with jpackage?
No, jpackage creates installers for the operating system it runs on, so use CI runners per platform.
Why sign and notarise desktop applications?
To prove publisher identity and avoid OS security warnings; macOS additionally requires notarisation for Gatekeeper to allow the app.

topics.name: Interview Questions: JavaFX Basics, Stage and Scene, FXML, Scene Builder, Binding and ObservableList

beginner.content:
How to answer

• Give a short definition, name the mechanism (scene graph, properties, FX thread), show a tiny code example, then state a pitfall (blocking the FX thread, listener leaks, null @FXML fields). Interviewers want to see that you build responsive, testable UIs.

intermediate.content:
Rapid-fire recap

QuestionAnswer
JavaFX vs SwingScene graph + CSS + FXML + binding, GPU rendering, actively developed
Stage / SceneWindow / its content (root node)
FXMLXML view description separate from controller logic
Scene BuilderVisual FXML editor
BindingProperty follows another (uni) or both sync (bi)
ObservableListList that notifies listeners; backbone of ListView/TableView

expert.content:
Follow-up questions to prepare

• "Why is my @FXML field null?" (id mismatch, missing @FXML, controller created with new, accessed in the constructor.) • "Unidirectional vs bidirectional binding, and what happens if you set a bound property?" (it throws.) • "How do you avoid listener leaks?" (remove or weak listeners, prefer bindings.) • "How do you structure a JavaFX app?" (MVVM: view in FXML, controller thin, view model with properties, services behind interfaces.)

interviewQA: What is JavaFX?
A Java framework for building rich desktop and embedded client applications using a scene graph, controls, CSS, FXML, animation, charts and media; distributed as OpenJFX.
JavaFX vs Swing?
JavaFX offers a GPU-accelerated scene graph, CSS styling, FXML, built-in properties/binding, animation and charts and is actively developed; Swing is a mature but maintenance-mode toolkit.
What are Stage and Scene?
A Stage is a top-level window; a Scene is the container for the scene graph displayed in a stage, holding the root node.
What is FXML?
An XML-based markup language for declaring the scene graph, loaded by FXMLLoader and wired to a controller using fx:id and event handler attributes.
What is Scene Builder?
A drag-and-drop visual designer that edits FXML files and can generate a controller skeleton.
What is property binding?
A mechanism where a property automatically follows another observable value (unidirectional) or two properties stay in sync (bidirectional), reducing manual listener code.
What is ObservableList?
A List that can be observed for changes (add/remove/update); UI controls such as ListView and TableView update automatically when it changes.
How do controllers communicate?
Through shared model objects with properties, parent-child controller references, callbacks or an event bus, instead of static references.
What happens in initialize() vs the constructor of an FXML controller?
The constructor runs before @FXML injection; initialize() runs afterwards when the nodes are available.
How do you style a JavaFX app?
With JavaFX CSS (-fx- properties) using style classes, IDs and pseudo-classes in external stylesheets applied to the Scene.

topics.name: Interview Questions: FX Thread, Task vs Service, TableView, Spring Boot Integration, Packaging and Background API Calls

beginner.content:
Scenario answers

• "The UI freezes when loading data" → the load runs on the FX thread: move it to a Task, bind a progress indicator, update the table in setOnSucceeded.
• "How do you call a REST API without freezing?" → Task/CompletableFuture on a background executor, error handling via setOnFailed, Platform.runLater or thenAcceptAsync(..., Platform::runLater) to update the UI.
• "How do you ship it?" → modular build, jlink runtime, jpackage installer per OS in CI, signed and notarised.

intermediate.content:
Cheat sheet

TopicRemember
FX threadOne thread for UI; never block it; update UI only there
TaskOne-shot; updateProgress/updateMessage; cancel cooperatively
ServiceReusable; restart(); createTask()
runLaterQueue work on the FX thread; don't flood it
TableViewFilteredList → SortedList → table; lambda cell value factories
Spring integrationContext in init(), controller factory, prototype controllers
Packagingjlink runtime + jpackage installer; sign and notarise

expert.content:
Deep-dive questions

• "How does Task.updateProgress avoid flooding the UI?" (it coalesces updates and posts one pending runLater.) • "What happens if you call Platform.runLater(...).get-style waits on the FX thread?" (deadlock.) • "How do you cancel a search-as-you-type request?" (Service.restart or cancel the previous Task/Future.) • "How do you get the Spring SecurityContext inside a Task?" (use DelegatingSecurityContextExecutor.)

interviewQA: What is the JavaFX Application Thread?
The single thread that processes UI events and renders pulses and is the only one allowed to modify the live scene graph.
Why should long-running tasks not execute on the UI thread?
They block event processing and rendering, freezing the entire application; run them in background threads and update the UI via Platform.runLater or Task callbacks.
What is the difference between Task and Service?
Task is a single-use background job; Service is a reusable factory that creates a new Task for each start/restart and manages its execution, suited to repeatable operations like refresh or search.
How does TableView work?
It shows an ObservableList of items; each TableColumn has a cell value factory to extract values and a cell factory to render them; rows are virtualised and reused while scrolling.
How do you filter and sort a TableView?
Use FilteredList with a predicate, wrap it in a SortedList bound to the table comparator and set it as the table items.
How do you integrate JavaFX with Spring Boot?

Start the Spring context in Application.init(), use the FXMLLoader controller factory to obtain controllers as Spring prototype beans, publish a stage-ready event from start() and close the context in stop().
How do you package a JavaFX application?
Build a modular or fat-jar app, create a minimal runtime with jlink and a native installer with jpackage per operating system, then sign (and notarise on macOS).
How do you handle background API calls?
Run them in a Task or CompletableFuture with timeouts and error handling on an executor, show progress, and apply results on the FX thread; cancel obsolete requests when the user navigates away.
How do you avoid memory leaks in JavaFX?
Remove listeners from long-lived properties, use weak listeners or bindings, stop animations and executors and avoid static references to controllers.
How do you test a JavaFX application?
Unit-test view models and services with JUnit 5/Mockito and write a few end-to-end UI tests with TestFX, headless on CI using Monocle.
