topics.name: Example: Login Form with Validation, Binding and a Background Task

beginner.content:
What you build

• A login window: username and password fields, a Login button that stays disabled until both fields are filled, an error label bound to the result, and a progress indicator while the (simulated) server call runs in a background Task. It uses layouts, properties/binding, events and concurrency together.

intermediate.content:
Step by step: what each part does

• Binding: login.disableProperty().bind(...isEmpty().or(...)) removes manual enable/disable code. • Task: the sleep runs off the UI thread; runningProperty() drives the spinner and prevents double submits. • Callbacks: setOnSucceeded runs on the FX thread, so touching the UI there is safe. • Daemon thread: the JVM can exit even if the task is still running.

expert.content:
Extending the example

• Add a "Show password" checkbox (bind a visible TextField's text bidirectionally to the PasswordField), a remember me value stored in Preferences, a shake animation on failure (TranslateTransition with cycle count), and replace the fake check with a RestClient call that returns a token.

interviewQA: How do you prevent a user from submitting a form twice?
Disable the button while the Task is running by binding its disableProperty to the task's runningProperty, and run the request off the FX thread.
Why bind instead of enabling the button in listeners?
Binding keeps the state derived from the inputs automatically and avoids missed update paths.

topics.name: Example: Course Manager with TableView, Search, Add and Delete

beginner.content:
What you build

• A table of courses with a search box (FilteredList), sortable columns (SortedList), an Add form below and a Delete button enabled only when a row is selected. It is the typical CRUD screen of a business desktop app.

intermediate.content:
Key ideas to notice

• The source list (data) is the only thing you modify; FilteredList and SortedList are views over it. • The comparator binding keeps header-click sorting working. • Bindings.size(filtered) keeps the counter live. • Properties in Course make cell edits and renames show instantly.

expert.content:
Making it production-ready

• Load and save through a repository inside a Task; show a placeholder (table.setPlaceholder); confirm deletes with an Alert; persist column widths; add pagination for large data; style rows by state with a row factory.

interviewQA: How do you combine filtering and sorting in a TableView?
Wrap the source list in a FilteredList, wrap that in a SortedList bound to the table comparator and set the SortedList as the table items.
Why modify the source list instead of the filtered list?
Filtered and sorted lists are read-only views; changes to the source propagate to them automatically.

topics.name: Example: CSV Import with Progress, Cancel and Error Handling

beginner.content:
What you build

• A screen that imports a CSV in the background: a FileChooser, a progress bar and status message bound to the Task, a Cancel button and a result list. It shows the correct way to keep the UI responsive while processing thousands of rows.

intermediate.content:
Design notes

• updateProgress / updateMessage coalesce updates so thousands of rows do not flood the FX thread. • Rejected rows are posted with Platform.runLater; for very many failures collect them in a list and publish once at the end. • Cancellation is cooperative: the loop checks isCancelled(). • Bindings are released when the task ends so the labels can be reused.

expert.content:
Scaling up

• Stream the file (Files.lines in a try-with-resources) instead of readAllLines for huge files; batch database inserts (500 rows per transaction); return a result object (ok, rejected, duration) instead of an int; offer a drag-and-drop target for the file; make the importer a plain class so it can be unit tested without JavaFX.

interviewQA: How do you let a user cancel a long import?
Run it in a Task, bind a Cancel button to the running state and check isCancelled() inside the loop.
Why not call Platform.runLater for every row?
It floods the FX event queue; use updateProgress/updateMessage (coalesced) or publish results in batches.

topics.name: Real-World Scenario: Shop Inventory Desktop App (Layers, Database, Background Sync, Offline)

beginner.content:
The scenario

• A shop owner uses a desktop app to manage products and stock, scan barcodes and sync with a head-office server. Requirements that shape the design: the UI must never freeze, data must survive a power cut, the app must work offline, and the team needs testable code. Architecture: View (FXML) → ViewModel (properties) → Service → Repository (SQLite) + SyncClient (REST).

intermediate.content:
Data safety and offline

• Use an embedded SQLite/H2 database with a transaction per stock change and a sync outbox table (pending changes). A ScheduledService pushes the outbox to the server when online; the stock update and outbox row are written in one transaction so a crash cannot lose or duplicate a change.

expert.content:
UX details that matter in a shop

• Barcode scanners type like a keyboard: capture key events on the scene, buffer characters and treat Enter as "scan complete". • Show a status bar bound to the view model (online/offline, pending changes). • Keep operations undoable where possible. • Test the view model with a fake service and a direct executor (Runnable::run) - no JavaFX needed.

interviewQA: How do you keep a desktop app responsive while saving to a database?
Run persistence in a Task on a background executor, bind busy/status properties for feedback and apply results in the succeeded callback.
Why write the stock change and the outbox row in one transaction?
So a crash cannot leave a stock change without a sync record (or vice versa), guaranteeing eventual synchronisation.

cheatNotes: Application - Base class every JavaFX app extends
start(Stage) - Entry point method JavaFX calls after launch()
Stage - The top-level window of a JavaFX application
Scene - The container of content placed inside a Stage
Scene Graph - Tree of Node objects that make up a Scene's visual content
Node - Base class for anything visual: buttons, labels, panes, shapes
VBox / HBox - Stack children vertically / horizontally
GridPane - Row-and-column layout, like an HTML table
StackPane - Layers children on top of each other
setOnAction() - Attaches a click handler to a control like Button
Property (e.g. textProperty()) - Observable, bindable wrapper around a value
bind() - Keeps one property automatically synced with another
FXML - XML-based markup for declaring JavaFX UIs separately from Java code
CSS styling - JavaFX supports CSS stylesheets for theming controls
launch(args) - Bootstraps the JavaFX runtime and calls start()
Platform.runLater() - Schedules code to run on the JavaFX Application Thread
